title.narrative: Supporting the reconstruction of communities social and financial resilience in war affected communities in Ukraine

description.narrative: Overall objective: Increase resilience of IDPs, local communities and institutions to conflict-related economic and social stresses.Intended impacts: (1) Labour market systems are strengthened through information provision and social partnerships,(2) Equitable access to employment opportunities is improved through learning market-relevant skills,(3) Entrepreneurship is enhanced through provision of financial and advisory services to MSMEs,Outcomes: (1)The labour market systems are strengthened through information provision and social partnerships,(2) Equitable access to employment opportunities is improved through learning market-relevant skills,(3) Entrepreneurship is enhanced through provision of financial and advisory services to MSMEs,

This project includes both IDP’s and host communities ensuring equitable access to income generation opportunities irrelevant of status within the population. The targeting within those groups will be tailored towards the and those who have been disproportionately negatively affected by the war. This includes women, age categories over 45, and people with disabilities. Targeting of financial support to SME’s will include businesses that have been disrupted, closed or relocated due to the war, and those that support identified key value chains within the labour market assessments.Criteria are a mix of socio-economic vulnerability criteria which consider willingness to participate in the project and the economic status in the households.At the end of the project, community target groups (working-aged men and women with a focus on females, those aged +45 and people with disabilities) as well as core labour market public and private sector stakeholders will have improved access to market linkages and essential information on relevant skills needed for employment programs and key labour market demands. By the end of the project, 845 TVET participants,460 interns and 250 individuals enrolled in the cash for work scheme, will have an improved access to employment opportunities and development of market-relevant skills , while employment opportunities and market growth are expanded for 200 micro enterprises and50 small and medium enterprises .

With WHH as the lead organisation to joint program, comprising of a shared staffing and country operational structure, the project is implemented under the umbrella of Joint Emergency Response Ukraine (JERU). JERU aims to support the reconstruction of communities’ social and financial resilience in war affected in East and West Ukraine. Additionally, this project will also work in partnership with Helvetas, an Alliance 2015 partner with his own Country office in Ukraine and who have a strong global focus on Economic Recovery and Livelihoods programming.
